title: Corning Museum of Glass turns LEGO's Classic Space astronaut into a giant glass sculpture
summary: The LEGO Group has shared a clip of glassblowers at the Corning Museum of Glass recreating the iconic Classic Space astronaut minifigure on a giant scale, though the piece itself isn't for sale.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group has shared an Instagram clip showing the Corning Museum of Glass crafting a giant glass version of the classic blue Classic Space astronaut minifigure. The museum has previously created oversized glass minifigures live in front of audiences, similar to the style of the 40649 Up-Scaled LEGO Minifigure set, but this is described as its first time tackling the specific Classic Space astronaut design.

The finished glass piece isn't available to purchase, so if you fancy an oversized astronaut for your own collection, the closest official option is the 40921 Up-Scaled Blue Astronaut Minifigure set, currently priced at £54.99 / $59.99 / €59.99.

## Why it matters
Classic Space is one of the most beloved and recognisable LEGO themes among collectors, so any fresh creative take on the astronaut minifigure is likely to catch fans' attention. It also highlights an ongoing collaboration between the LEGO Group and the Corning Museum of Glass, showing how brick-inspired designs can be reimagined in completely different mediums and craft traditions.

- **More plant personalities** – building on Cosy Plants' theme of hobbies, with ideas like painting, gaming, or music-loving plants.
- **Seasonal plants** – Christmas, Halloween or Valentine's-themed versions with festive accessories.
- **More interchangeable accessories** – letting fans mix and match parts across different Botanicals sets more freely, such as giving a Rocking Plant a book or a Happy Plant a lie-down pose.

None of these ideas are confirmed – they're fan and press speculation about the future direction of the range.

Botanicals has become a popular, collectable little range for LEGO fans who enjoy display pieces and character-driven builds. A new official set landing in November gives collectors something concrete to look forward to, while the wishlist highlights just how much appetite there is for the range to expand – useful context for anyone building or displaying their own plant collection alongside official sets.

title: Rumour: LEGO Icons 11388 'Venice Neighbourhood' could be a 5,682-piece set
summary: A mystery LEGO Icons set is rumoured to be a huge Venice-themed build with over 5,600 pieces, potentially the brand's biggest Italian city tribute yet.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to a rumour reported by Brick Fanatics, a mystery LEGO Icons set numbered 11388 and nicknamed 'Venice Neighbourhood' could be coming in November 2026. It's said to feature 5,682 pieces and a price around $549.99 / €499.99. None of this is confirmed by LEGO Group, so treat it as speculation for now.

If accurate, this would dwarf previous LEGO Italy-inspired sets. The current benchmark, 21359 Italian Riviera, has 3,251 pieces and packs in plenty of architectural detail and coastal charm. Venice is a much bigger, more complex subject, so fans are naturally wondering whether even 5,682 pieces is enough to do the city justice.

Interestingly, the fan and custom building community may already have answered that question. Official-adjacent set 910023 Venetian Houses uses 3,470 pieces to capture iconic Venice features like canals, gondolas and bridges, while independent builder JPNG created a detailed Venice-style MOC with under 3,000 pieces, complete with open-back buildings, interiors and a bridge. These examples suggest a well-designed set could nail the Venice look without needing the full rumoured piece count.

## Why it matters
Big city-themed LEGO Icons sets are popular with collectors and display builders, and a Venice set at this scale would be one of the largest of its kind. For fans of custom brick building and MOCs, it's also a useful reminder that clever design can rival huge piece counts when it comes to capturing a location's character.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for official confirmation from LEGO Group on set number, name, piece count and price, as none of these details have been verified yet. If confirmed, expect more images and details closer to a possible November 2026 release.

title: LEGO Ideas 21373 Downton Abbey: the story behind its minifigures
summary: LEGO designers have explained the thinking behind the 13 minifigures included in the Downton Abbey Ideas set, including new prints and a brand-new piece.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas 21373 Downton Abbey, a 4,711-piece set priced at £269.99, launches on 1 October. Ahead of release, LEGO's design team spoke to fan media about how the set's 13 minifigures were chosen and designed.

Design Manager Jordan David Scott explained that the team worked with fan designer Sebastian, plus licensing partners Highclere Castle's Lord and Lady (who advised on the building's architecture) and NBCUniversal (who own the show), to decide which characters made the final line-up.

According to Scott, choosing outfits was trickier than choosing characters, given how many looks each character has across the series. The team settled on smart ballroom wear to keep things elegant, and gave standout characters new face prints, name-checking Maggie Smith's character and Carson's distinctive eyebrows as examples. Some figures also get extra head accessories, while the male characters were simpler to design since their suits are broadly similar.

The set also includes a brand-new piece, though specific details on what it is weren't given in this excerpt.

## Why it matters
Minifigure selection and printing are often the biggest talking points for licensed LEGO Ideas sets, and this kind of designer insight helps collectors understand the choices behind a set before buying. It's also a good example of how licensing negotiations with multiple rights holders can shape what fans ultimately get in the box.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for full reveals of the new piece and prints once 21373 Downton Abbey is available from 1 October, along with reviews covering the minifigure lineup in detail.

title: LEGO Ideas reveals why Downton Abbey's minifigures can finally sit down

Scott suggested this is a practical short-term solution rather than a permanent design standard, hinting that a more advanced 'foldable hip' style piece could be developed by other teams in future, though nothing concrete has been confirmed.

## Why it matters
Seated minifigures wearing skirts or dresses have long been a tricky design challenge, often limiting how characters can be displayed. Communities such as the LEGO Batman subreddit have been discussing how the model's exterior could be reworked into Wayne Manor, with ideas floating around for reusing minifigures as Court of Owls members or Thomas and Martha Wayne.

## What happened

The LEGO Ideas team has officially confirmed that 92 fan-submitted projects have reached the second 2026 review stage, after gathering the required 10,000 supporters. None of the qualifying projects were disqualified before the deadline. The lineup covers a wide mix of themes, from film and TV tie-ins to original concepts, and each will now be assessed by a review panel to see if any deserve to become official LEGO sets.

Looking ahead, any project that hits 10,000 supporters up to 4 January 2027 will move into the third 2026 review, which is reportedly already gaining strong momentum. Results from the earlier first 2026 review are expected to be announced this autumn.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few official routes for fan concepts to become real, mass-produced sets, so confirmation of qualifying projects is a big deal for the community members behind them and for fans hoping to see their favourite ideas hit shelves. For collectors and builders, it's also a useful early look at what themes could be coming in future waves of official releases.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out this autumn for the first 2026 review results, and watch which of the 92 second-round projects get selected to move forward towards a potential official LEGO release.
